questions.prompt: As of Next.js 15, what is the default caching behavior of fetch()?

options.text: Not cached — fresh on every request unless you opt in
Cached for exactly 60 seconds by default
Never allowed to be cached at all

questions.explanation: In Next.js 15, fetch is uncached by default. You opt into caching with cache: 'force-cache' or next: { revalidate }.

questions.prompt: To cache a fetch response indefinitely until revalidated, pass cache: '______'.
questions.explanation: cache: 'force-cache' caches the response until it is revalidated; 'no-store' never caches.

questions.prompt: Which trigger an immediate (on-demand) refresh of cached data? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: revalidatePath and revalidateTag invalidate cached data immediately. next: { revalidate } is time-based, and a reload doesn't clear the server cache.

questions.prompt: Match each caching option to its effect.
questions.explanation: no-store is always fresh, force-cache caches indefinitely, revalidate does timed refresh (ISR), and revalidateTag invalidates on demand.

questions.prompt: Order the lifecycle of a tagged, hourly-revalidated blog list after a new post is created.

items.text: The list is fetched with next: { revalidate: 3600, tags: ['posts'] }
Visitors are served the cached list quickly
A Server Action creates a post and calls revalidateTag('posts')
The next request rebuilds and serves the fresh list

questions.explanation: The tagged fetch is cached and served fast; revalidateTag invalidates it after the mutation, so the next request regenerates the fresh list.
